messages.subject: Formatting data for csvToUMF() function
parts:
Hello! I'm writing my master thesis with bird point-count data and want to use Single season-single species occupancy modelling. However, I can't get the csvToUMF()-function to work properly, so I can't really start...

I know that it should look like this:
csvToUMF(filename, long=FALSE, type, species, ...)

and I have looked at the example for long format, which I believe my data is in:
head(read.csv(system.file("csv","frog2001pcru.csv", package="unmarked")))

dat1 <- csvToUMF(system.file("csv","frog2001pcru.csv", package="unmarked"),
                 long = TRUE, type = "unmarkedFrameOccu")

I have also checked p. 18 in the unmarked instruction document, where it is specified what a correctly formatted long-table should look like. But even after this, I get an error saying:
Error in read.table(file = file, header = header, sep = sep, quote = quote,  : 'file' must be a character string or connection

This is what I use for the"file"-input in the csvToUMF-function:

testUMF <- csvToUMF(read.csv("C:/Users/PC/Documents/Examensarbete/Data/Focusdata_2019_RBS_test.csv", header = T, sep = ";", dec = ".", quote=""),

                 long = TRUE, type = "unmarkedFrameOccu")


I have tried changing the "sep" and "dec", but I arrived at the conclusion that ; for sep and . for dec is correct. I also tried putting my data directly on the C:/ to shorten the filename. I have restarted R, and so on. Nothing works.


I am also wondering if it is necessary to use Juliandate for the 2nd column, or if normal date is ok? On p. 18 it just says "date", but in the pcru-frog-example the dates are in Julian format. I have never heard of Julian format before.


Thank you in advance!!


/Panicking MSc student

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Formatting data for csvToUMF() function
parts:
Krisztina,

csvToUMF is expecting just a string with the filename, not a call to read.csv(), as the first argument. This results in a different problem because csvToUMF cannot handle CSVs that have separators that are anything but "," and as you note your  file has ";. Finally, as Andy notes, the missing values in the dates are problematic.

Luckily I think there are some quick workarounds:

library(unmarked)

inp <- read.csv('Focusdata_2019_RBS_test.csv',sep=';') #read in file with non-standard separator

inp <- inp[!is.na(inp$Date)&!is.na(inp$RBS_freq), ] #Remove rows with missing values

fl <- formatLong(inp, type='unmrakedFrameOccu') #Convert data frame to UMF

fl #look at resulting  UMF

occu(~1~Crop+Wood, data=fl) #test fitting model

Here above in the formatLong() function, I get a warning saying "attributes are not identical across measure variables; they will be dropped". What does this mean? Also, when looking at the new variable "fl"", I'm not sure it is converted correctly. According to my idea, my obsCovs are the weather variables (Wind, Rain, Cloud) and my siteCovs are the habitat data (Crop, Wood, Scub, etc.). I'm unsure if the function understands this. I'm also unsure what y1, y2 and y3 are in my case. Shouldn't this mean that the sites were surveyed 3 times? In reality they were surveyed either once or twice. Same thing with rain 1, rain 2, rain3, and so on.

Warning message number 2 comes in this part:

#Fit detection models
#Function is: occu(~detectability cov ~occupancy cov, data)
dm1 <- occu(~1 ~1, fl) #Null model
dm2 <- occu(~ Wind ~ 1, fl)
dm3 <- occu(~ Cloud ~ 1, fl)
dm4 <- occu(~ Wind + Cloud ~ 1, fl)

The warning message is:

In truncateToBinary(y): Some observations were > 1.  These were truncated to 1.


I interpret this as the format should be binary (presence-absence, 0/1), but I have frequencies of RBS (bird species Red-backed shrike). Is it possible to keep it as frequencies, or is it unimportant/unnecessary? I was just thinking that seeing for example 5 RBS at one site means that the result would be a higher occupancy than seing 1. However, with binary data, this kind of "gets lost" in the process, if you understand what I mean. I get the same warning when I proceed to put in occupancy covariates, for example:

om2 <- occu(~ Wind + Cloud ~ Crop, fl)

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Formatting data for csvToUMF() function
parts:
You have at least one site (AP_E09) that has 3 observations:

table(inp$Point_ID)

Perhaps that is a mistake in the raw data, if you change it to the correct Point_ID and run formatLong, you should end up with only two observations.

You can use
siteCovs(fl)

and
obsCovs(fl)

to look and check if it looks like they have been read in right. To be honest I would advise against using csvToUMF or formatLong, and rather read the documentation for unmarkedFrameOccu() carefully and build the frame manually yourself to make sure it's exactly how you want it.

You're correct that your counts are being truncated to 0/1 every time you run a occu model. There are similar types of models for count data, e.g. N-mixture models which can be fit with the pcount() function in unmarked. There are advantages and disadvantages to this vs. occupancy models that depend on your research questions, experimental design, and dataset. I would suggest you look at the relevant chapters of one of the available textbooks, e.g. Marc & Andy's "Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology" to help you decide which fits your situation best.

Ken
